status: Draft reading summaries for owner review; original abstracts and bibliographic records are unchanged.
source_policy: Owner-reviewed summaries use supplied abstracts where present. Other publications without supplied abstracts use title/type-based scope descriptions, except other-12, whose CRAF description is verified against the official GAIP report page.

entries.refereed-25: Interpretable neural networks estimate mortality quantiles while retaining the structure of classic stochastic mortality models. The framework supports stochastic mortality simulation and longevity-linked derivative pricing.
entries.refereed-24: This modelling study connects land-use and land-cover changes in Southeast Asia with air pollution, health outcomes and economic costs. It estimates excess deaths and associated losses through both biogeophysical and biogeochemical pathways.
entries.refereed-23: The study quantifies persistent life-expectancy losses from El Niño across high-income Pacific Rim countries, estimating monetary-equivalent losses of US$2.6 trillion and US$4.7 trillion for the 1982–83 and 1997–98 events. Under moderate emissions pathways, projected losses reach US$35 trillion by 2100.
entries.refereed-22: This chapter reviews the actuarial foundations, empirical evidence and practical design of index insurance for climate and weather risks. It also discusses potential applications of artificial intelligence and blockchain.
entries.refereed-21: A kernel principal component extension of the Lee–Carter model captures nonlinear patterns in mortality data. Empirical tests examine forecasting performance and uncertainty, including during the COVID-19 pandemic.
entries.refereed-20: The paper develops pandemic bonds and endemic swaps to finance severe pandemic outbreaks and recurrent epidemics. Coronavirus and dengue examples illustrate pricing with epidemiological and actuarial models.
entries.refereed-19: Using data from 335 regions in China, this study examines how digital financial inclusion affects domestic tourism demand. Spatial panel models identify effects within regions and spillovers across regions.
entries.refereed-18: A neural network embedded in a utility-maximization framework designs weather index insurance and endogenously determines premiums and demand. The approach captures nonlinear weather–loss relationships to reduce basis risk and improve welfare.
entries.refereed-17: This mortality forecasting framework combines neighbouring prediction, model ensembling and tree boosting. Tests using the Human Mortality Database examine long-horizon prediction and the benefits of pooling information across populations.
entries.refereed-16: A count-based frequency–severity framework models cyber events and data breaches, accounting for dependence, zero inflation and heavy tails. The estimation approach is applied to the Privacy Rights Clearinghouse dataset.
entries.refereed-15: The paper models and prices storm catastrophe bonds using loss distributions and spatial–temporal dependence. Florida county-level data illustrate how the proposed bonds can hedge reinsurers’ storm losses.
entries.refereed-14: A deep factor model combines an autoencoder and convolutional neural networks to forecast crop yields. An application to Iowa data evaluates forecasting accuracy and implications for crop insurance ratemaking.
entries.refereed-13: A neighbouring prediction framework treats mortality tables as two-dimensional images, enabling convolutional neural networks to learn intricate nonlinear patterns across ages and years. Evaluations cover 41 countries and regions, with an extension to multiple populations.
entries.refereed-12: A multi-factor exponential extension of Gompertz mortality modelling accommodates flexible age patterns, including at very old ages. The study evaluates historical fit, forecasting and a multi-population extension.
entries.refereed-11: A dynamic factor model summarizes many explanatory variables to forecast crop yields and design weather index insurance. Illinois crop data are used to assess prediction accuracy, basis risk and hedge effectiveness.
entries.refereed-10: A hidden Markov chain approximation makes Bayesian premiums tractable in insurance models with dynamic unobserved policyholder risk. Numerical and real-data examples evaluate its accuracy and pricing flexibility.
entries.refereed-09: The study compares principal component regression and partial least squares regression for constructing multivariable weather insurance indices. Ontario forage data illustrate how dimension reduction can address multicollinearity and basis risk.
entries.refereed-08: The paper compares thirteen pasture production indices, including satellite-derived vegetation and biophysical measures, for predicting forage losses. Alberta pasture observations provide a validation testbed for remote-sensing applications in insurance.
entries.refereed-07: A relational data-matching model borrows loss experience from similar regions when farm-level yield data are unavailable. Canadian and U.S. corn data are used to assess yield predictions and premium-rate estimates.
entries.refereed-06: A multivariate weighted premium principle reweights historical agricultural losses using external risk information. Manitoba reinsurance data illustrate its pricing implications and allocation of loadings across risk layers.
entries.refereed-05: A credibility-based crop yield model combines weather information and production data across geographically correlated regions. The resulting framework supports reinsurance pricing and weather risk management.
entries.refereed-04: A Lévy subordinated hierarchical Archimedean copula (LSHAC) model captures spatial dependence in weather risks to support agricultural hedging. The analysis examines basis risk, downside protection and the effects of spatial aggregation.
entries.refereed-03: A Lévy subordinated hierarchical Archimedean copula (LSHAC) framework models mortality dependence across countries and is evaluated using data from thirteen countries. A survival index swap example illustrates the role of dependence in longevity risk and population basis risk.
entries.refereed-02: The paper develops the theory and estimation procedure for Lévy subordinated hierarchical Archimedean copula (LSHAC) models. Exchange-traded fund data illustrate applications to tail dependence and Value-at-Risk estimation.
entries.refereed-01: An Erlang mixture model and a modified credibility approach are used to price crop reinsurance. Canadian crop insurance data are used to assess tail fit and liability-weighted loss-cost experience.
entries.other-13: A technical report on cyclone risk in the Asia Pacific and its future outlook.
entries.other-12: The report proposes a Climate Risk Adjustment Factor (CRAF) to incorporate climate effects into mortality tables, supporting insurers’ climate stress testing and forward-looking risk assessment in Asia.
entries.other-11: A technical report on the lasting effects of climate anomalies on mortality and health in the United States.
entries.other-10: A technical report on modelling inland flood risk in Southeast Asia.
entries.other-09: A magazine article discussing El Niño and climate-related economic challenges in Southeast Asia.
entries.other-08: A technical report discussing the relevance of sea-level rise to the insurance sector.
entries.other-07: A newspaper article discussing how a record-breaking El Niño could affect economic growth in Southeast Asia.
entries.other-06: A response to Gerber and Shiu’s discussion of the proposed premium principle for agricultural insurance.
entries.other-05: A response to Abylay Zhexembay’s discussion of the proposed premium principle for agricultural insurance.
entries.other-04: A technical report on predictive analysis of technology, weather and crop yields.
entries.other-03: A technical report assessing forage insurance based on satellite-derived biophysical parameters in Alberta, Canada.
entries.other-02: A technical report assessing forage insurance based on satellite-derived biophysical parameters in Saskatchewan, Canada.
entries.other-01: A technical report on forecasting farm-level crop yields when farm-level data are unavailable.
entries.working-01: Longevity shocks affect corporate term spreads and debt maturity through changes in life insurers’ demand for bond duration.
entries.working-02: The paper develops joint significance tests for high-dimensional linear regression with heteroskedastic and dependent errors. Random matrix theory and self-normalization provide inference without requiring a known sparsity level or error-dependence structure.
entries.working-03: A neural stochastic differential equation framework jointly models mortality, interest rates and housing conditions for reverse mortgage valuation. Forecasting and simulation results inform a Monte Carlo pricing engine for tenure-payment contracts.
entries.working-04: A behaviour-based machine learning framework forms risk pools for area-yield insurance using utility maximization and spectral clustering. U.S. corn and soybean data are used to evaluate basis risk, tail risk and contract performance.
entries.working-05: A geographically structured deep learning model captures spatial dependencies in flood hazards to inform insurance pricing. Mississippi River Basin data and an application to the National Flood Insurance Program are used to evaluate hazard estimates, premiums and capital requirements.
entries.working-06: The paper uses longevity shocks to identify duration-hedging stock trades by pensions and life insurers. It examines how these trades relate to momentum and contrarian trading patterns.
entries.refereed-26: A two-stage framework optimizes carbon credits and subsidies to support green-project viability, then links policy-adjusted cash flows to green bond pricing. It examines how complementary policy instruments affect project solvency and the value of the green attribute.

refereed-23.source: Existing supplied abstract and NTU research release
refereed-23.note: US$2.6T/4.7T historical monetary-equivalent losses and US$35T by 2100 under moderate emission pathways; not GDP estimates.

other-12.note: Formal expansion: Climate Risk Adjustment Factor; base-table adjustment, industry stress testing and forward-looking risk assessment.
